title: Rung 1 -- coverage of one generated triangle against Cycles, no light model in the comparison

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- rung 1 of the ten scenes: one triangle at about 30 % of the frame under a declared camera

acceptanceClass.because: A right-isoceles triangle, fronto-parallel, rolled by -arctan(1/2) and scaled so that all three edge constants sit at half a lattice step (doc/requirements.md I.26.14). The subject was an EQUILATERAL triangle and could never carry this: an equilateral triangle's interior angles are 60 deg, so if one edge's raster slope is rational the other two are tan(t +/- 60 deg) = (t -/+ sqrt3)/(1 +/- t*sqrt3), irrational for every rational t -- no roll makes its silhouette rational, and the measured slope residual against the admissible family was 4.51 px. The section's construction is written for THIS shape and names it, so the shape is what was wrong.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: THE EXACTNESS CONSTRUCTION OF doc/requirements.md I.26.14, AND NOT I.26.10'S FRAMING RULE -- the two are separate determinations of the camera distance and a case carries exactly one. FRONTO-PARALLEL: the subject is a plane at z = 0 and the eye sits on the plane's own normal, so the perspective image of it is a SIMILARITY and the raster slopes are the subject's own, rotated by the roll and by nothing else. ROLL -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg: tan(45 deg + t) = (1+t)/(1-t) and tan(90 deg + t) = -1/t stay rational whenever tan t does, so a rational roll keeps this right-isoceles silhouette rational -- the three edges come out at raster slopes -1/2, 2 and 1/3, i.e. lines -1x-2y=c, 2x-1y=c and 1x-3y=c with |n| = sqrt5, sqrt5 and sqrt10, whose margin ceilings are 0.223606797749979, 0.223606797749979 and 0.158113883008419 px. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. SCALE: with the leg 1 m and k px per metre at the plane's depth, the rotated triangle is V0 + (4a, -2a) and V0 + (-2a, -4a) at a = k/(2*sqrt5), which is s = 2a in the section's own notation. The three constants satisfy -c01 - c02 + c12 = 10a identically -- a combination the normals annihilate, so no aim can change it -- and half-lattice on all three therefore needs 10a = 1/2 (mod 1). a = 176.05 satisfies it, giving s = 352.1, the section's own choice, and the reason for that value rather than another admissible one is vertical slack: the rotated bounding box is 6a x 4a = 1056.3 x 704.2 px inside 1280 x 720. k = 10a/sqrt5 = 787.31953487767589 px per metre and the depth at which one metre subtends k px is (720/2)/(0.24*k) = 1.905198503975964 m. AIM: at the subject's own bounds centre the three constants are -2238.75, 39.25 and -439.00, so none is at a half step and the third is at a whole one -- the worst case, an edge through every pixel centre it meets. The raster shift that fixes both free constants is the unique solution of -Tx - 2Ty = 1/4 and 2Tx - Ty = 1/4 modulo 1 nearest the vertical centring, Tx = 0.05 px and Ty = -176.15 px, and the third follows from the identity. Converted through the same similarity it is an aim of (-0.10011360408974723, -0.20008520306731042) m, which places the three vertices at raster (463.5, 711.5), (1167.7, 359.4) and (111.4, 7.3) -- all inside 1280 x 720, and every one of the three constants exactly at half a lattice step. THE CLAIM IS RECOMPUTED, NOT TRUSTED: the runner measures both conditions from the projected geometry and refuses this class if either fails. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) and the clip range [0.1, 100] m are Blender's factory camera, measured from a --factory-startup scene: lens 50 mm, sensor height 24 mm, clip_start 0.1 m, clip_end 100 m.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Diffuse BSDF with Roughness pinned to 0, never Principled: Principled at metallic 0 still carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5. This subject is a single unoccluded facet, which is the one shape where Cycles has no integration left and the answer is the closed form rho*L = 0.8 x 0.05087608844041824 = 0.0407008707523346 -- so this is one of the cases that keeps that number exercised (doc/requirements.md I.26.13).

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

notes: Rung 1's subject is generated here rather than fetched (doc/requirements.md I.26.5 row 1), so a red at rung 1 has exactly one cause: every vertex is ours and none of them came from a file. Its geometry is Khronos's Triangle's -- legs of 1 m along +X and +Y -- and that is deliberate rather than accidental: with render/coverage/fetched-triangle carrying the same shape under its own construction, the ONE difference between the two cases is generated against fetched, and a red on exactly one of them names which. It carries NORMAL as well as POSITION even though a coverage comparison reads neither, because the alternative -- admitting a normal-less vertex for one fixture -- is a shape change to the engine bought by a test.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices; exact because the subject is a plane perpendicular to the optical axis, so its perspective image is a similarity and the area is 10*a^2 = 309936.025 px^2 at a = 176.05 px. That is 33.630211 %, which is the section's own figure for this construction and is above its 30 % floor
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
